title: The local registry script cannot publish a prerelease, which is every build between releases
foundBy: using the script to hand a consumer agent a build of an unreleased commit

evidence.verified:
Reproduced first: with package.json at a prerelease version, `npm run registry:local` exited non-zero on the publish step with npm's prerelease-tag error, after staging had succeeded. With the fix, the same command exits 0 and reports "Publishing to http://localhost:4873/ with tag dev".

There is no unit test. This repository tests its CLI scripts by running them, as `scripts/dev-version.test.mjs` does with `spawnSync`. Running this one boots verdaccio and publishes, which is too much to put in `npm test` for a dev-only script. The verification above is the execution, and it covers both the failing and the fixed case.

details:
`scripts/local-registry.mjs` publishes with `npm publish .package --access public` and no `--tag`. npm refuses a prerelease without one: "You must specify a tag using --tag when publishing a prerelease version."

Every version between two releases is a prerelease. `scripts/dev-version.mjs` produces `0.3.1-dev.<stamp>.<sha>`, which is the shape the publish workflow uses, so the script worked only when package.json carried a plain release version. That is the one case a developer is least likely to be testing: the point of the script is to rehearse a publish of work in progress.

The fix publishes under the `dev` tag when the version is a prerelease, matching the dist-tag the workflow uses. So `npm install <name>@dev` reaches a local build the way it would reach a published one.
